events.title: Charlemagne Dies
events.description: Charlemagne, King of the Franks and the first Holy Roman Emperor, died in Aachen at about age 71. His son Louis the Pious succeeded him as ruler of the Frankish Empire.
events.significance: Charlemagne had united much of western Europe. His reign shaped medieval politics, religion and culture, and he is often called the 'Father of Europe'.

events.title: Death of Henry VIII
events.description: Henry VIII of England died at age 55. His nine-year-old son became King Edward VI.
events.significance: Henry broke England from Rome and created the Church of England. His death opened a period of religious and political upheaval in Tudor England.

events.title: Sir Francis Drake Dies at Sea
events.description: Sir Francis Drake, the English seaman and explorer, died of dysentery off the coast of Panama. He was about 50.
events.significance: Drake was the first Englishman to circumnavigate the globe. He also helped defeat the Spanish Armada in 1588, which made him a symbol of English naval power.

events.title: Space Shuttle Challenger Disaster
events.description: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launching from Cape Canaveral, Florida. All seven crew members were killed.
events.significance: The tragedy led to a long grounding of the shuttle fleet and a major investigation. It also led to lasting changes in NASA's safety culture and decision-making.
